title: Beyond the male prototype: A systematic review of female psychopathy in forensic populations.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review examines the assessment of psychopathy in female populations, critically analyzing the psychometric performance of traditional instruments compared to newer dimensional models, while exploring the distinct phenotypic and behavioral characteristics of psychopathy in women.
METHOD: A comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify empirical studies evaluating psychopathy in women across forensic and correctional settings.
RESULTS: The evidence reveals that traditional behavioral and criminal indicators-such as those operationalized by the Psychopathy Checklist-Revised (PCL-R)-systematically yield lower scores in women. This has often resulted in the controversial and potentially arbitrary lowering of diagnostic cutoff scores for female samples. Furthermore, the review identifies key differential characteristics in female psychopathy, noting that women tend to exhibit higher rates of relational aggression, verbal hostility, and emotional dysregulation over overt physical violence. Conversely, alternative dimensional frameworks, such as the Psychopathic Personality Traits Scale (PPTS), the Comprehensive Assessment of Psychopathic Personality (CAPP), and the DSM-5 Alternative Model for Personality Disorders (AMPD), demonstrate robust validity. These models successfully capture the core personality traits, emotional dysregulation, and high Cluster B comorbidity characteristic of female psychopathy without relying on explicit antisocial history.
CONCLUSION: Traditional instruments present limitations in reflecting how psychopathy manifests in women. Transitioning toward dimensional personality frameworks is essential to ensure gender-sensitive and clinically useful assessments.
